rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Distressed Asset Renewal Surge" (identical renewal leg, with lct/act simply swapped for dlc/lt inside the same SUMRANK distress conditioner already used in "Soft-Asset Rollover Fragility"), so it tests no new economic channel and is dominated by the archive's stronger "Renewal Funding Shortfall."

Both legs are increasing in capex (acceleration of capx/ppent and the capx-minus-oancf gap), so the product is largely a monotone repackaging of high capital spending rather than a genuine conditional interaction, and it recombines legs already tested in "Cash-Flow-Strained Capex Acceleration" and "Renewal Funding Shortfall."

The signal is essentially the well-known asset-growth anomaly (PP&E plus inventory expansion) crossed with the same distress conditioner already used in at least four archived signals, and its two component channels were separately tested in "Demand-Mismatched Capacity Build" and "Liquidity-Strained Inventory Build."

This is a mechanical leg swap—the exact stale-inventory leg from "Stale Inventory Leverage Overhang" paired with the exact SUMRANK(dlc/lt, NEG oancf/at) conditioner from "Soft-Asset Rollover Fragility"—with no new mechanism and a high likelihood of simply reproducing the earlier alpha.

Leg one is verbatim from "Soft-Asset Rollover Fragility" and leg two verbatim from "Renewal Funding Shortfall," and because intangible-intensive firms typically have low capex the funding-gap conditioner is likely to be a weak, largely orthogonal (or even attenuating) modifier rather than a substantive refinement.

This is a legitimate functional-form repair of the unstable sstk/(capx+aqc) denominator in "Dilutive Noninvestment Rescue" with a coherent hypothesis and matching sign, though it reuses the identical distress conditioner and sits close to the known share-issuance/external-finance anomaly, limiting its novelty.
